cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Partitioning divides a large table into smaller pieces, by rows (horizontal) or by columns (vertical), so queries can skip irrelevant data and old data is easy to drop.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Sharding is horizontal partitioning across servers, scaling storage and writes beyond one machine but making cross-shard joins, transactions and rebalancing harder. The key decision is the partition key: it must match the main access pattern and spread load. Range partitioning suits ordered data like dates.

questions.q: If you shard by hash of user ID, is load guaranteed even?
questions.a: No. Data spreads evenly, but one very active key like a celebrity or big tenant can still create a hot shard.
For ordered data like dates or numeric ranges, such as sales by month.
Splitting a table by columns, each partition holding a subset of columns.
